results.label: A:cutoff
results.title: cutoff construction
results.statement:
For every $g\in\CH$: $K(g)=H_0+V(g)$ is essentially self-adjoint and bounded below; its closure
(again denoted $K(g)$) has $E(g)=\inf\spec K(g)$ as a \emph{simple} eigenvalue, and the
normalized eigenvector $\Om_g$ may be chosen strictly positive $d\phi_0$-a.e.\ in $Q$-space.
For every real $h\in L^1\cap L^2$ of compact support, $V(h)$ is self-adjoint on its maximal
multiplication domain.

\emph{Wick powers of the time-zero field} (added 7 November 2026; the construction behind
$V(h)$ of \S\ref{subsec:model}).  Let $\HH_C$ be the real Hilbert space obtained by
completing the real-valued $\mathcal S(\R)$ in the inner product $2\ip f{Cg}$ ($C$ is bounded and
strictly positive, so this is an inner product, and $\mathcal S(\R)$ is a dense continuously
imbedded subspace, $2\ip f{Cf}\le\|f\|_2^2/m_0$).  $Q$-space with $d\phi_0$ and $\varphi_0$ is
the Gaussian random process indexed by $\HH_C$ in the source's normalisation, ``(c)
$\langle\phi(v)\phi(w)\rangle=\frac12\langle v,w\rangle$, the inner product on $\mathcal H$''
\cite[Definition, p.~15]{SimonBook}: $(\varphi_0(f))_f$ is a centred Gaussian family with
$\E[\varphi_0(f)\varphi_0(g)]=\ip f{Cg}$; such a process is determined by its index space up to
isomorphism \cite[Thm.~I.6, p.~15]{SimonBook}.  The
source's definitions are used as printed.
\emph{(a)}~For Gaussian random variables $f_1,\dots,f_k$, ``The Wick product
${:}f_1^{n_1}\cdots f_k^{n_k}{:}$ is defined recursively in $n\equiv n_1+\dots+n_k$ by
${:}f_1^0\cdots f_k^0{:}=1$, $\langle{:}f_1^{n_1}\cdots f_k^{n_k}{:}\rangle=0\,(n\ne0)$ and
$\frac{\partial}{\partial f_i}{:}f_1^{n_1}\cdots f_k^{n_k}{:}=n_i\,{:}f_1^{n_1}\cdots
f_i^{n_i-1}\cdots f_k^{n_k}{:}$'' \cite[p.~12]{SimonBook}; for one variable,
${:}f^n{:}$ is the coefficient of $\alpha^n/n!$ in ${:}\exp(\alpha f){:}=\exp(\alpha
f-\frac12\alpha^2\langle f^2\rangle)$ \cite[(I.15), (I.18a), p.~10]{SimonBook}, explicitly
${:}f^n{:}=\sum_{m=0}^{[n/2]}\frac{n!}{m!\,(n-2m)!}\,f^{n-2m}\bigl(-\tfrac12\langle
f^2\rangle\bigr)^m$ \cite[(I.18b), p.~10]{SimonBook}.
\emph{(b)}~$\langle{:}f^n{:}\;{:}g^m{:}\rangle=\delta_{nm}\,n!\,\langle fg\rangle^n$ for
jointly Gaussian random variables $f,g$ \cite[Thm.~I.3, (I.21), p.~11]{SimonBook} (its proof
uses that $\alpha f+\beta g$ is Gaussian; every use below is within one Gaussian process), and
$\langle{:}f_1\cdots f_n{:}\;{:}g_1\cdots g_m{:}\rangle=0$ if $n\ne m$
\cite[Cor.~I.4, (I.23a), p.~12]{SimonBook}.
\emph{(c)}~$\Gamma_n(\HH)$ is ``the closed subspace[\,] generated by
$\{{:}\phi(f_1)\cdots\phi(f_n){:}\mid f_i\in\mathcal H\}$'' \cite[p.~16]{SimonBook} (p.~17
says ``spanned by''), with $\Gamma(\HH)=L^2(d\phi_0)$ for $\HH=\HH_C$; by (b) the spaces
$\Gamma_n$, $n\ge0$, are mutually orthogonal, $\Gamma_0$ being the constants.
\emph{(d)}~For $n\ge1$ and $g\in L^{1+\varepsilon}(\R)$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the Wick power
${:}\varphi_0^n(g){:}_C$ is ``the unique random variable in $\Gamma_m(\HH)$ with
$\langle{:}\phi(h_1)\cdots\phi(h_m){:},{:}\phi^m(g){:}\rangle=m!\int[\prod_{j=1}^mh(x_j)
S(x_j,y)]g(y)\,dx\,dy$'' \cite[(V.3), p.~136]{SimonBook} (printed with $h(x_j)$ where
$h_j(x_j)$ is meant [sic]), taken with $m=n$, $\HH=\HH_C$ and the kernel $S$ of the
source's (V.1), ``$\frac12\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal H}=S(f\otimes g)$'' \cite[p.~134]{SimonBook},
which for the inner product $2\ip f{Cg}$ of $\HH_C$ is $S(x,y)=C(x-y)$, the kernel of
$\ip\cdot{C\,\cdot}$ (Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-kernel}); that is,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl\langle{:}\varphi_0(f_1)\cdots\varphi_0(f_n){:},\,{:}\varphi_0^n(g){:}_C\bigr\rangle
 =n!\int\Bigl[\prod_{j=1}^n\int f_j(x_j)\,C(x_j-y)\,dx_j\Bigr]g(y)\,dy
 \qquad(f_j\in\mathcal S(\R)) .
 \tag{W.1}\label{eq:wickpairing}
\end{equation}
It exists for this class: ``${:}\phi_F^n{:}$ exists for any $n$ as a random process for
$L^{1+\varepsilon}(R)$ for each $\varepsilon\,\epsilon\,(0,1]$.  Moreover, for any such
$\varepsilon$ and any $p\ge2$, $\|{:}\phi_F^n(g){:}\|_p\le c(p-1)^{n/2}\|g\|_{1+\varepsilon}$
(V.6b)'' \cite[Thm.~V.2(b), p.~138]{SimonBook}, with $\|{:}\phi^m(g){:}\|^2=m!\int
g(x)g(y)S(x,y)^m\,dx\,dy$ \cite[p.~137]{SimonBook}.  The source prints (V.3) for
$g\in\mathcal S$ and says ``If the map $g\mapsto{:}\phi^m(g){:}$ from $\mathcal S$ to
$\Gamma_m(\mathcal H)$ extends to a larger test function space, $X$, than $\mathcal S$ we say
${:}\phi^m{:}$ exists for $X$'' \cite[p.~136]{SimonBook}: for $g\in L^{1+\varepsilon}$,
${:}\varphi_0^n(g){:}_C$ is that extension, continuous for $\|\cdot\|_{1+\varepsilon}$ by
(V.6b) at $p=2$, and \eqref{eq:wickpairing} persists for it, both sides being continuous in
$g$ (the right side by H\"older's inequality, since $\prod_j\int f_j(x)C(x-\cdot)\,dx$ is
bounded and integrable for $f_j\in\mathcal S(\R)$, $C\in L^1(\R)$); an element of
$\Gamma_n(\HH_C)$ is determined by its pairings with the Wick monomials with $f_j\in\mathcal
S(\R)$, as the source's ``unique'' in (V.3) asserts.  For $n=0$ and $g\in L^1(\R)$,
\eqref{eq:wickpairing} with the empty product determines the constant
${:}\varphi_0^0(g){:}_C:=\int g$; it is not continuous for $\|\cdot\|_{1+\varepsilon}$, and
(V.6b) is used only for $n\ge1$.  Every real $h\in L^1\cap L^2$ of compact support lies in
$L^{1+\varepsilon}(\R)$, so $V(h)=\lambda\sum_na_n{:}\varphi_0^n(h){:}_C$ of
\S\ref{subsec:model} is defined, real, and linear in $h$.

\emph{Sources.} \cite[p.~588]{GJS}; existence and uniqueness of the cutoff vacuum:
\cite[Thms.~2.2.1, 2.3.1]{GJ2}; lower bounds and positivity: \cite{GJ71}; the semigroup
construction: \cite[Thm.~5.3]{Rosen70}; the Wick powers: \cite[pp.~10--12, 15--17,
134--138]{SimonBook}, read on the page images on 7 November 2026.

\emph{Scope.} Strict positivity of $\Om_g$ is the standard positivity-improving semigroup
argument of the cited construction; simplicity is used below only through the two consequences
$c_g:=\ip{\Om_g}{\Om_0}>0$ and the absence of a second ground vector. \emph{Isolation of
$E(g)$ (a gap) is not imported}; the gap of \S\ref{sec:G} is an output.
Of the Wick powers: the facts (a)--(c) are printed in Chapter~I for the Gaussian process
indexed by any real Hilbert space, and the definition (V.3) for a real Hilbert space
$\mathcal H$ containing $\mathcal S_R(R^n)$ as a dense continuously imbedded subspace, with the
kernel $S$ of (V.1) locally integrable \cite[pp.~134--135]{SimonBook}; $\HH_C$ satisfies these
hypotheses (above), and $C$ is locally integrable (Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-kernel}).  The
normalisation of the source's ``time zero Minkowski field'' $\phi_F$ of Theorem V.2(b) was not
re-checked; its existence statement and (V.6b) are used for $\phi_F$ read as the process
indexed by $\HH_C$.  For bounded $h$ of compact support, the only $h$ for which a proof below
uses $V(h)$ (the general statements of this assumption, of Assumption~\ref{A:domain}(i) and of
Proposition~\ref{prop:smoothing} are applied only to such $h$), the same
element is constructed in this manuscript as an explicit $L^2(d\phi_0)$-limit
(Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-ident}(iii) with Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-wick}(iii)), so nothing
below rests on that reading alone.  The sources of the cutoff construction define $V(g)$ by
normal ordering in Fock space; that their $V(g)$ is the object defined here is the Fock
space--$Q$-space dictionary of \cite[Ch.~I]{SimonBook}, a reading of the kind recorded in
Assumption~\ref{A:gjs}, Scope~(d).

\emph{Used in.} \S\ref{subsec:model} (the construction and locality of $V(h)$),
\S\ref{sec:slab} (slab limits), \S\ref{sec:M2} (Step~1; weak-graph passage),
\S\ref{sec:G} (density, spectral projections), \S\ref{sec:path} (simple Perron root),
\S\ref{sec:ground} and \S\ref{sec:dichotomy} (covariance and parity via
Lemma~\ref{lem:covparity}), Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} (Lemma~\ref{lem:Z} uses item (c)),
Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} (Lemmas~\ref{aux:notation-wick} and~\ref{aux:notation-ident}).

results.label: A:fkn
results.title: Feynman--Kac--Nelson transfer
results.statement:
Let $d\mu_0$ be the free Euclidean Gaussian measure with covariance
$(-\Delta_{\R^2}+m_0^2)^{-1}$, $J_t$ the sharp-time embeddings, and, for $h\in\CE$,
$\mathcal U_h:=\lambda\int h(z){:}\mathscr P(\Phi(z)){:}\,dz$. For all bounded time-zero
functions $f,h'$, $T>0$, and $g\in\CH$,
\[
 \ip{f}{e^{-TK(g)}h'}
 =\int\overline{(J_Tf)}\,(J_0h')\,e^{-\mathcal U_{\mathbf 1_{[0,T]}\otimes g}}\,d\mu_0 ,
\]
with the interaction over exactly the slab $[0,T]$ carrying the two embeddings, together
with the analogous multi-time formulas on finite slabs (used in \S\ref{sec:slab} in the
two- and one-time forms, where the symmetric slab cutoffs
$h_{T,g}:=\mathbf 1_{[-T,T]}\otimes g\in\CE$ enter through the \emph{normalized}
measures $dq_{h_{T,g}}$).

\emph{Sources.} Free-field FKN: \cite[Thm.~III.6]{SimonBook}; interacting form:
\cite[Cor.~V.14, Thm.~V.15]{SimonBook}; equivalently \cite[Thms.~II.14, II.16]{GRS75}.

\emph{Scope.} \cite[Thm.~III.12]{SimonBook} is a projection-product estimate, % negative-scope mention (whitelisted): III.12
\emph{not} an FKN theorem, and is nowhere used (audit finding S1).
The identification of sharp-time Wick functionals with $Q$-space multiplication operators is
the conventions lock, Remark~\ref{rem:conv}.

\emph{Used in.} \S\ref{sec:slab} (slab identities), \S\ref{sec:M2} (Step~1: the sharp-time
embedding $J_0$), \S\ref{sec:path} (path formula), Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} (through
Lemma~\ref{aux:d1-cov}(i)), Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}.

{\raggedright\emph{Dossier.} \texttt{simon-free-fkn-111}, \texttt{simon-fkn-184/185},
\texttt{grs-fkn-39/40}, \texttt{simon-wrong-iii12-119} (E27--E43 range).\par}

results.label: A:stability
results.title: finite-volume stability
results.statement:
For every $h\in\CE$: $\mathcal U_h\in L^p(d\mu_0)$ for every $p<\infty$, and
$e^{-\varrho\,\mathcal U_h}\in L^1(d\mu_0)$ for every finite $\varrho>0$. In particular
$0<Z(h):=\int e^{-\mathcal U_h}d\mu_0<\infty$, and the interacting measures
\[
 dq_h:=Z(h)^{-1}e^{-\mathcal U_h}\,d\mu_0 ,\qquad h\in\CE ,
\]
are well-defined probability measures.

\emph{Construction of $\mathcal U_h$} (added 7 November 2026; repair R8 of the V3 audit,
Appendix~\ref{app:provenance}).  Let $\HH_G$ be the real Hilbert space obtained by
completing the real-valued $\mathcal S(\R^2)$ in the inner product
$2\ip f{(-\Delta_{\R^2}+m_0^2)^{-1}g}$; $(\mathcal S'(\R^2),d\mu_0,\Phi)$ of
Assumption~\ref{A:fkn} is the Gaussian random process indexed by $\HH_G$ in the source's
normalisation (as for $\HH_C$ in Assumption~\ref{A:cutoff}), so that the kernel of (V.1) is
$G(z-z')$ of Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-kernel}(v), which is locally integrable.  The
Wick products, the pairing facts and the chaoses $\Gamma_n(\HH_G)\subseteq L^2(d\mu_0)$ are
those of Assumption~\ref{A:cutoff}, items (a)--(c), for $\HH=\HH_G$; for $n\ge1$ and $g\in
L^{1+\varepsilon}(\R^2)$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the Wick power ${:}\Phi^n(g){:}$ is the
unique element of $\Gamma_n(\HH_G)$ with
\begin{equation}
 \bigl\langle{:}\Phi(f_1)\cdots\Phi(f_n){:},\,{:}\Phi^n(g){:}\bigr\rangle
 =n!\int\Bigl[\prod_{j=1}^n\int f_j(z_j)\,G(z_j-z)\,dz_j\Bigr]g(z)\,dz
 \qquad(f_j\in\mathcal S(\R^2)),
 \tag{W.2}\label{eq:wickpairingE}
\end{equation}
\cite[(V.3), p.~136]{SimonBook} (for $g\notin\mathcal S$ the continuous extension, as in
Assumption~\ref{A:cutoff}(d)); it exists for this class, ``${:}\phi^n{:}$ exists for any
$n$ as a random process for $L^{1+\varepsilon}(R^2)$ for each $\varepsilon\,\epsilon\,(0,1]$''
\cite[Thm.~V.2(a), p.~137]{SimonBook}, with
\begin{equation}
 \|{:}\Phi^n(g){:}\|_{L^2(d\mu_0)}^2=n!\iint g(z)\,g(z')\,G(z-z')^n\,dz\,dz'
 \tag{W.3}\label{eq:wickisometry}
\end{equation}
\cite[p.~137]{SimonBook}, and, for every $p\ge2$, $\|{:}\Phi^n(g){:}\|_p\le
c\,(p-1)^{n/2}\|g\|_{1+\varepsilon}$ with $c$ depending on $\varepsilon$ and $n$ only
\cite[(V.6a), p.~137; Remark~1, p.~138]{SimonBook}.  For $n=0$ and $g\in L^1(\R^2)$,
\eqref{eq:wickpairingE} with the empty product gives the constant ${:}\Phi^0(g){:}:=\int g$,
as in Assumption~\ref{A:cutoff}(d); the bound above is used only for $n\ge1$.  Every
$h\in\CE$ is bounded with compact support, hence in $L^1\cap L^{1+\varepsilon}(\R^2)$, and
\[
 \mathcal U_h:=\lambda\sum_{n=0}^{2p'}a_n\,{:}\Phi^n(h){:}\in\bigoplus_{n=0}^{2p'}\Gamma_n(\HH_G),
 \qquad {:}\Phi^0(h){:}=\int h\,dz ,
\]
which is linear in $h$ and lies in every $L^p(d\mu_0)$ by (V.6a); this makes the first clause
of the assumption a consequence of the construction, and the clause on
$e^{-\varrho\,\mathcal U_h}$ is the import proper.  Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} shows that
$\mathcal U_h$ is the $L^2(d\mu_0)$-limit of its mollified versions
(Lemma~\ref{lem:uv} with Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-ident}(iii)).  The second quantization of a
contraction $c$ on $\HH_G$ acts on the Wick monomials by $\Gamma(c)\,{:}\Phi(f_1)\cdots
\Phi(f_n){:}={:}\Phi(cf_1)\cdots\Phi(cf_n){:}$ \cite[(I.32), p.~25]{SimonBook}; in
particular $\Gamma(e^{-t}\mathbf 1)$ is multiplication by $e^{-nt}$ on $\Gamma_n(\HH_G)$.

\emph{Source.} The first clause: \cite[Thm.~V.2(a), (V.6a), p.~137]{SimonBook}; the
second, with $P:=\varrho\lambda\mathscr P$ (semibounded, since $\varrho\lambda\ge0$ and
$a_{2p'}>0$) and $g:=h\ge0$: \cite[Thm.~V.7(a), (V.28a), p.~152]{SimonBook}
(``Let $P$ be a fixed semibounded polynomial. Then (a) If $g\ge0$, $g\,\epsilon\,L^1\cap
L^{1+\epsilon}(R^2)$, then $\exp(-\int g(x){:}P(\phi(x)){:}d^2x)\,\epsilon
\bigcap_{p<\infty}L^p(Q_N,d\mu_{0,N})$'', dossier image \texttt{simon-exp-174})
and its chapter context; the construction: \cite[pp.~135--137]{SimonBook}, read on the page
images on 7 November 2026 (until then the assumption cited Theorem V.7 for both clauses and
stated no construction; V3 audit, findings M-3 and m-9).

\emph{Scope.} Only finite slabs and compactly supported $h$ occur below; no infinite-volume
stability is imported. A self-contained quantitative lower bound on $Z(h)$ and the
$h$-uniform $L^p$ bound on $e^{-\mathcal U_h}$ are proved in Appendix~\ref{app:huniform}
from the construction above and Assumption~\ref{A:hyper}.  That the source's
$\int g\,{:}P(\phi){:}$ in Theorem V.7 is the $\mathcal U_h$ constructed from its own (V.3)
is read off the chapter (both are built on the same Wick powers); that it is the $V(h)$ of
\cite[(1.8), p.~589]{GJS}, which prints ``Wick order with respect to the measure $d\Phi$''
and no construction, is a reading of the kind recorded in Assumption~\ref{A:gjs},
Scope~(d).

\emph{Used in.} \S\ref{sec:reduction} (Lemma~\ref{lem:classes}), \S\ref{sec:slab},
\S\ref{sec:path} (H\"older/Vitali chains), Appendix~\ref{app:huniform},
Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}.

{\raggedright\emph{Dossier.} \texttt{simon-exp-174}, \texttt{simon-transfer-178/179/180} (E33--E43 range);
construction of $\mathcal U_h$ (added 7 November 2026): \texttt{simon-wickdef-156/157/158},
\texttt{simon-wickthm-159}, \texttt{simon-secondq-047}.\par}

results.label: A:hyper
results.title: free hypercontractivity
results.statement:
The free time-zero Markov semigroup $\mathsf P_T$ satisfies
\[
 \|\mathsf P_TF\|_{q}\le\|F\|_{p}
 \qquad\text{whenever}\qquad \frac{q-1}{p-1}=e^{2m_0T},\quad 1<p\le q<\infty .
\]

More generally (the abstract form of the same source): for the second quantization
$\Gamma(c)$ of a contraction $c$ on the one-particle space of any Gaussian $L^2$-space,
$\|\Gamma(c)F\|_{q}\le\|F\|_{p}$ whenever $\|c\|^2\le(p-1)/(q-1)$; the display is the
case $c=e^{-T\mu}$, and the Mehler case $c=e^{-t}\mathbf 1$ on $L^2(d\mu_0)$ is the form
used in Appendix~\ref{app:huniform}.

\emph{Sources.} \cite[Thm.~I.17]{SimonBook} (the abstract form and the display); the
time-region form is \cite[Thm.~III.17]{SimonBook}.  The moment comparison on the chaoses
that Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} derives from the abstract form is also printed as
\cite[Thm.~I.22, (I.47), p.~38]{SimonBook}: ``if $\psi\,\epsilon\bigoplus_{n=0}^m
\Gamma_n(\mathcal H)$, then $\|\psi\|_p\le(p-1)^{m/2}\|\psi\|_2$ for all $p>2$'' (read on
the page image on 7 November 2026).

\emph{Scope.} \cite[Thms.~V.10, V.12]{SimonBook} are, respectively, a transfer-matrix % negative-scope mention (whitelisted): V.10, V.12
application and an essential-self-adjointness theorem; neither is the hypercontractivity input
and neither is cited for it (audit finding S2).  The abstract form is printed for
$p,q\in(1,\infty)$, $p\le q$ \cite[Thm.~I.17, p.~34]{SimonBook}; every use below has
$1<p\le q<\infty$ (\S\ref{sec:path}, Step~1: $p=1+e^{-m_0T}$; Appendices~\ref{app:huniform}
and~\ref{app:comparison}: $p=2$).  How $\Gamma(c)$ acts on the chaoses, (I.32), is recorded in
Assumption~\ref{A:stability}.

\emph{Used in.} \S\ref{sec:path} (the pairing bound), Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} (tail
estimate; the comparison $\|Y\|_q\le(q-1)^{p'}\|Y\|_2$), Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}
(the same comparison at $q=4$).

{\raggedright\emph{Dossier.} \texttt{simon-hyper-056}, \texttt{simon-timeslice-125/126};
Theorem I.22 (added 7 November 2026): \texttt{simon-thm122-060}.\par}

results.label: A:domain
results.title: domain smoothing; common core
results.statement:
\emph{(i)} For every $g\in\CH$ and $t>0$,
\[
 \Ran e^{-tK(g)}\subseteq D(H_0)\cap D(V')
\]
for every polynomial multiplication operator $V'$ of the time-zero field with coefficients in
$L^1\cap L^2$ of compact support (in particular for every $V(h)$ as in
\S\ref{subsec:model}).
\emph{(ii)} For every affine path $g_s=(1-s)g+sg'$, $g,g'\in\G$, there is a common core
$\mathscr C$ for all $K(g_s)$, $s\in[0,1]$, on which
$K(g_s)\xi=K(g_{s_0})\xi+(s-s_0)V(g'-g)\xi$.

\emph{Sources.} (i) is the model-specific smoothing theorem \cite[Ch.~7, Thm.~7.4]{GJExp}.
(ii) is part of the cutoff construction; essential self-adjointness pinpoints, in their
roles per the audit: \cite[Thm.~V.12]{SimonBook}, \cite[Thm.~5.3]{Rosen70}, \cite{GJ2}. % whitelisted: V.12 in its audited positive role (esa), not the S2 misuse

\emph{Scope.} \cite[Thm.~7.3]{GJExp} alone assumes a potential bounded below % negative-scope mention (whitelisted): Thm. 7.3
and is therefore \emph{not} sufficient here; the citation is to Theorem~7.4
(audit finding S3).

\emph{Used in.} Proposition~\ref{prop:smoothing}, \S\ref{sec:slab} (dominators),
\S\ref{sec:path} (eigenvalue differentiation).

results.label: A:patch
results.title: free propagation; patching; the dynamics $\alpha$
results.statement:
\emph{(i)} The free dynamics $\mathrm{Ad}\,e^{itH_0}$ has propagation speed one
(Klein--Gordon finite propagation), and the Trotter product formula for $e^{itK(g)}$ converges
strongly.
\emph{(ii)} There is a one-parameter automorphism group $\alpha$ of $\A$, independent of $g$,
with
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_t(\A(O))\subseteq\A(O_{|t|}),\qquad
 \alpha_t(A)=\beta^g_t(A)\ \ \text{if } g\equiv1 \text{ on } O_{|t|}\ (A\in\A(O)).
 \tag{P}\label{eq:P}
\end{equation}
\emph{(iii)} The net is local: $\A(O)\subseteq\A(O')'$ for disjoint bounded open intervals
$O$, $O'$ (listed on 7 November 2026; used before without being listed).

\emph{Sources.} \cite[\S III]{GJ1}; \cite[\S\S3.5--3.6]{GJ2}; \cite[\S4.1 and Ch.~4]{GJExp};
(iii): \cite[p.~397, proof of Thm.~3.5.1]{GJ2}, read on the page image on 7 November 2026.

\emph{Scope.} \eqref{eq:P} is the Glimm--Jaffe patching construction verbatim; the
$g$-uniform propagation bound for the \emph{cutoff} dynamics is not imported but derived
(Proposition~\ref{prop:propagation}).  Item (iii) is printed for the algebra the source
defines, for an open set in space, ``as the weak closure of the bounded functions of the
$t=0$ fields'' $\int\varphi(x,0)f(x)\,dx$ and $\int\pi(x,0)f(x)\,dx$ ``as $f$ runs over the
$C^\infty$ functions with support in'' that set: for two ``disjoint open sets'', ``elements
of'' the two algebras ``commute''.  The algebra so defined for an interval $O$ is the
$\A(O)$ of \S\ref{subsec:model}, which is generated by the bounded Borel functions of
$\varphi_0(f)$ and $\pi_0(f)$, $f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ real, once the source's Fock-space fields
$\varphi(x,0)$, $\pi(x,0)$ are read as the $Q$-space fields $\varphi_0$, $\pi_0$: the Fock
space--$Q$-space dictionary of the Scope paragraph of Assumption~\ref{A:cutoff}, a reading of
the source.  Items (i) and (ii) are imported under the same reading.  (Until 7 November 2026

on $W(f,0)$ and $W(0,h)$ enters
$\sigma_s(\A(O))=\A(sO)$.)

\emph{Used in.} Proposition~\ref{prop:propagation}, \S\ref{sec:filter} (locality identity),
\S\ref{sec:lppl}, \S\ref{sec:ground}; item (iii): \S\ref{subsec:model} (\emph{Locality}, hence
Proposition~\ref{prop:propagation} and the two-regime bound of \S\ref{sec:lppl}) and
\S\ref{sec:dichotomy} (Step~1 of the proof of the dichotomy theorem).

results.label: A:covar
results.title: covariance data
results.statement:
Let $U_a$ implement the space translation $\tau_a$ on $Q$-space and let
$\Theta:=\Gamma(-1)$, so that $(\Theta\psi)(q)=\psi(-q)$ in $Q$-space. Then, for every
$g\in\CH$,
\[
 U_aK(g)U_a^*=K(\tau_ag),\qquad \Theta H_0\Theta=H_0,\qquad
 \Theta V(g)\Theta=V(g)\ \ \text{for even }\mathscr P .
\]

\emph{Sources.} \cite[p.~398]{GJ2} (cutoff covariance); the transformation of Wick powers
under $\Gamma(-1)$ is the parity of the polynomial.

\emph{Scope.} Only the displayed operator identities are imported; the state-level
consequences are derived in Lemma~\ref{lem:covparity}.

\emph{Used in.} Lemma~\ref{lem:covparity}; thence \S\ref{sec:ground},
\S\ref{sec:dichotomy}.

{\raggedright\emph{Dossier.} \texttt{gj2-cutoff-independence-38} (E06).\par}

results.label: A:gjs
results.title: the GJS package
results.statement:
The Euclidean input is \cite{GJS}, used exactly as printed, as follows.

\emph{(i) Measures.} For $h\in\CE$, $dq_h=Z(h)^{-1}e^{-\mathcal U_h}d\mu_0$ as in
Assumption~\ref{A:stability}; the Hamiltonian cutoff class of \cite[(1.6), p.~588]{GJS} is
$\CH$.

\emph{(ii) Observable class.} The class (1.1.5) of \cite{GJS} consists of sharp-time monomials
$Q(x^0)=\int d\vec x\,w(\vec x)\prod_i{:}\Phi(x_i)^{m_i}{:}$ with $L^2$ kernels; equal times
are allowed, and products of individually Wick-ordered powers are admissible without
reordering.  Equation (1.1.6) of \cite{GJS}, $Q=\int dx^0\,Q(x^0)$, defines the
time-integrated monomials with kernels in $L^2$ of space-time; ``localized'' is defined for
both forms by support in a product of unit lattice squares ``centered at the lattice side
[sic] $j_i\in\mathbb Z^2$'' (p.~593), i.e.\ squares centred at integer points.  The spatial
cells used in \S\S\ref{sec:M2}--\ref{sec:norms} are the columns $[k-\frac12,k+\frac12)$,
$k\in\Z$, of these squares (Definition~\ref{aux:notation-squares} fixes the convention on
the lattice lines); the count bounds used below (at most three columns for a support of
length $2$, Theorem~\ref{thm:M2}, Step~2; $N_I\le\lfloor L\rfloor+2$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:cells}) are proved on them.  (Until 7 November 2026 these sections counted
in the cells $[j,j+1)$, a lattice shifted by one half unit, on which the displayed norm bounds
of Proposition~\ref{prop:gjsnorms} can fail for the norm of p.~594; Appendix~\ref{app:provenance},
corrections history.) GJS bound the degree of each \emph{individual} Wick factor: $n_i<\bar n$ for a fixed
finite $\bar n$, any choice $\bar n\ge\deg\mathscr P$ being sufficient; the printed text
adds ``Since there is no restriction on $r$, $Q$ still may have an arbitrarily large
degree'' (p.~593). Footnote~9 permits $\bar n=\infty$ at the price
$N(\Delta)!\to(N(\Delta)!)^3$ in (1.1.7), (1.1.8), (2.4.5). Every observable used below
has individual factor degrees $\le\max(2p',1)$, so the fixed finite choice
$\bar n=2p'+1$ applies and the printed first-power weights are used as displayed; the
\emph{total} degrees of the observables of \S\ref{sec:G} are unbounded, exactly as the
printed sentence licenses.

\emph{(iii) Printed norms.}
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 \textup{(1.1.7)}\ \ \|Q\|_{\rm GJS}=K_1\Bigl[\prod_\Delta K_2^{2N(\Delta)}N(\Delta)!\Bigr]\|w\|_2,\\
 \textup{(1.1.8)}\ \ \|Q(x_0)\|_{\rm GJS}=K_1\Bigl[\prod_\Delta K_2^{2N(\Delta)}N(\Delta)!\Bigr]\|w(x_0,\cdot)\|_2,
\end{gathered}
 \label{eq:printednorm}
\end{equation}
where $N(\Delta)$ is the total degree localized in the unit square $\Delta$, and
\textup{(1.1.9)}: a nonlocalized polynomial is normed by summing its localized pieces.
Replacing $K_2$ by $\max\{1,K_2\}$ only enlarges right-hand sides; \emph{we fix $K_2\ge1$}.

\emph{(iv) CE2.}
\begin{srcfact}[CE2 $=$ {\cite[Thm.~1.1.7]{GJS}}, p.~594]\label{sf:CE2}
For localized monomials $Q_1,Q_2$ with disjoint localization squares separated by a strip of
width $d$ bounded by two parallel lines (any orientation),
\[
  \Bigl|\int Q_1Q_2\,dq_h-\int Q_1dq_h\int Q_2dq_h\Bigr|\le C_7e^{-m_1d}\|Q_1\|_{\rm GJS}\|Q_2\|_{\rm GJS} ,
\]
with $m_1>0$ and $C_7$ \emph{independent of $h$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$} (so stated in the source).
\end{srcfact}

\emph{(iv-T) The transverse case, listed separately (A8(iv)-T; added 7 November 2026).}
GJS Theorem 1.1.7 is printed for localized monomials separated by a strip of any
orientation (p.~594). Its printed proof rotates the strip into the time direction
(p.~597) and so reaches sharp-time monomials only across strips parallel to the time-zero
line. Lemma~\ref{lem:ce2strip} uses only that case; Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} also uses
the transverse case, listed separately as A8(iv)-T.  Namely, \emph{A8(iv)-T} is Source
Fact~\ref{sf:CE2} applied to a sharp-time monomial $Q_1$ of type (1.1.5) and a localized
monomial $Q_2$ across a strip that is not parallel to the time-zero line (transverse in the
sense of Definition~\ref{aux:notation-stripdef}), at every $h\in\CE$: a case of the printed
statement that its printed proof does not reach (Scope, point (b)).  In every use that a
proof of this manuscript makes (Theorem~\ref{thm:D4}), $Q_2$ is of type (1.1.6) and the strip
is bounded by two lines of constant $x^1$.  It is
listed for transparency, not as a different import standard: it is the printed statement
at its printed scope, exactly as items (i)--(iv).  It is not a narrower form of the retired
item (vi): that was a moment bound on the slab class and stated no clustering, and neither
statement is known to imply the other.  Used in Theorem~\ref{thm:D4} (through
Lemma~\ref{lem:D2}), hence in Theorem~\ref{thm:M2} and in every statement that consumes its
constant $M$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:localize} onward); not in \S\ref{sec:G}, whose
Theorem~\ref{thm:D3} uses parallel strips only.

\emph{(v) CE1 (provenance; not used since 7 November 2026).}
\begin{srcfact}[CE1 $=$ {\cite[Thm.~1.1.8]{GJS}}, p.~595]\label{sf:CE1}
The printed estimate is
\[
 \bigl|\int Q(x^0)\,dq_h\bigr|\le C_8\|Q(x^0)\|_{\rm GJS},
\]
stated uniformly as the source cutoff tends to one.  This item records the literal
one-sentence statement of Theorem 1.1.8.  The cutoff-uniform form that \S\S\ref{sec:M2}
and~\ref{sec:G} consumed until 7 November 2026 was item~(vi), read off the printed Theorem
1.1.11 (p.~596) in the specialization the source itself prints as its proof of Theorem 1.1.8
(p.~600); since that date the moment bounds are Theorems~\ref{thm:D3} and~\ref{thm:D4} of
Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}, proved from item (iv) with items (i)--(iii),
Assumptions~\ref{A:fkn}--\ref{A:hyper} and Appendix~\ref{app:huniform}, and neither this item
nor (vi) is consumed by any proof.
\end{srcfact}

\emph{(vi) The cutoff-uniform moment estimate $U_{\rm GJS}$ (GJS Theorem 1.1.11 at
$B=I$, $n=0$; imported as printed from 31 October 2026; \textbf{retired on 7 November
2026}: no proof of this manuscript uses it; the item, its tag and its label are kept for
provenance).}
For
\[
 \CE^{\rm slab}:=
 \{h_{T,g}=\mathbf1_{[-T,T]}\otimes g:T>0,\ g\in\CH\}\subset\CE,
\]
one and the same constant $C_8$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\int Q(x^0)\,dq_{h_{T,g}}\right|
 \le C_8\|Q(x^0)\|_{\rm GJS}
 \quad(T>0,\ g\in\CH) .
 \tag{$U_{\rm GJS}$}\label{eq:UGJS}
\end{equation}
The quantifiers include every affine cutoff
$g_s=(1-s)g+sg'$ used later, because $g_s\in\CH$.  Equation
\eqref{eq:UGJS} was the CE1 uniformity needed in \S\S\ref{sec:M2} and \ref{sec:G} until
7 November 2026 (Theorems~\ref{thm:D3} and~\ref{thm:D4} now supply what those sections
need, from item (iv) and the inputs listed in Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}); from 31 October 2026 it was read off one printed theorem of the
source, as follows.
\begin{srcfactstar}[{\cite[pp.~596, 600 and 629]{GJS}}]
\emph{(a) p.~596.} ``We let $A$ and $B$ denote monomials of type (1.1.5) of degree $|A|$
and $|B|$ and with kernels $w_A$ and $w_B$ respectively. We assume that $A$ is localized at
times $x_{i0}\le0$, and that $B$ is localized at times $x_{i0}\ge0$. Let $B_T$ denote the
translate of $B$ at time $T>0$, so that $B_T$ is localized at times $\ge T$.''
``In the next two results, we take all times $x_{1,0}=t=\dots=x_{r,0}$ equal in $Q(x_0)$.
To indicate this restriction, we write $Q(t)$ in place of $Q(x_0)$.'' [\dots]
``\textsc{Theorem} 1.1.11. Let $n$ and $\varepsilon>0$ be given and let
$\gamma=(n+1)m_0(1-\varepsilon)$. For any $A$, we may choose $n$\textsuperscript{th} degree
polynomials $Q_n(t_j)$ of the form (1.1.5) with $r=1$, so that
\[
 \textup{(1.1.14)}\qquad \sum\nolimits_{t_j>0}e^{\gamma t_j}\|Q_n(t_j)\|\le O(1)\|A\|
\]
and so that
\[
 \textup{(1.1.15)}\qquad Q=\sum\nolimits_{0<t_j<T}Q_n(t_j)
\]
satisfies
\[
 \textup{(1.1.16)}\qquad \Bigl|\int(A-Q)B_T\,dq_h\Bigr|\le O(1)\|A\|\,\|B\|\,e^{-\gamma T} ,
\]
uniformly in $h$. We shall choose $t_j=j$, $j\in\mathbb Z$.''
\emph{(b) p.~600.} ``Proof of Theorem 1.1.8, assuming Theorem 1.1.10 [sic]. Choose $T=0$
and $B=I$ in Theorem 1.1.11. Then $Q=0$, so Theorem 1.1.8 is a special case of Theorem
1.1.10 [sic].''
\emph{(c) p.~629.} ``Theorem 1.1.11 follows from this inequality, while Theorem 1.1.8 is the
special case $B=I$, $n=0$.''
\end{srcfactstar}

\emph{Reading (vi) off the source fact.}  Take $n=0$ and $B=I$ in Theorem 1.1.11, as the
source does on p.~600 ($B=I$, $T=0$) and names on p.~629 ($B=I$, $n=0$).  For $0<T<1$ the sum (1.1.15) over the integers
$0<t_j<T$ is empty, so $Q=0$ and $I_T=I$, and (1.1.16) reads
$|\int A\,dq_h|\le O(1)\|A\|\,\|I\|\,e^{-\gamma T}\le O(1)\|A\|\,\|I\|$, uniformly in $h$,
for every monomial $A$ of type (1.1.5) localized at times $\le0$; the source's own choice
$T=0$ (p.~600) gives the same bound, and $0<T<1$ is used here because the source introduces
$B_T$ for $T>0$.  By (1.1.7)--(1.1.8), $\|I\|=K_1$ (no Wick factors: the product is empty and the kernel is
the constant $1$), so
\eqref{eq:UGJS} holds with
\[
 C_8:=O(1)\,K_1 ,
\]
$O(1)$ the constant of Theorem 1.1.11 at $n=0$ and a fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$; it holds for
every $h\in\CE$, in particular on $\CE^{\rm slab}$, and $C_8$ depends on the printed
thresholds only.  Three remarks make the reading exact.  \emph{(1)} A sharp-time monomial at
an arbitrary time $x^0$ is carried to a time in $(-1,0]$ by an integer time translation,
which maps the lattice squares of p.~593 onto themselves, preserves the norms
(1.1.7)--(1.1.8), the class $\CE$ and the measure $d\mu_0$, and carries $dq_h$ to $dq_{h'}$
with $h'$ the translated cutoff; the bound at $h'$ is the bound at $h$.  \emph{(2)} A general
$Q(x^0)$ with kernel of bounded support is a finite sum of localized monomials, and
$\|Q(x^0)\|_{\rm GJS}$ is the sum of their norms by (1.1.9); the bound is applied to each
piece, whose times are all equal, as the source requires for Theorems 1.1.10--1.1.11
(p.~596).  \emph{(3)} The smallness
hypotheses under which Theorem 1.1.11 holds are not printed in its statement; the source
prints them with Theorem 4.1, from which Theorems 1.1.8 and 1.1.11 are proved on pp.~628--629
(``Let $m_0$, $K_2$ and $K_1$ be sufficiently large, and let $\lambda$ be sufficiently
small''), and on p.~600 (``convergence of our expansions requires both sufficiently small
$\lambda$ and sufficiently large $m_0$''); \S\ref{subsec:weak} fixes the working constants
accordingly.  The admissibility of the degree-zero $B=I$ rests on the source's own use of it
(pp.~597, 600, 629) and on p.~593's ``there is no restriction on $r$''.

\emph{(vii) Printed corroboration of (vi).}
\begin{srcfact}[{\cite[p.~629, \S4]{GJS}}]\label{sf:printed}
``It is important to work with a translation invariant Hamiltonian, in order that time
translation preserve subspaces of bounded momentum. The estimates of Theorems 1.1.8, 1.1.11,
3.1 and 4.1 are uniform in the space cutoff $h$, and the path space integrals converge as
$h\to1$. Thus these theorems hold in the infinite volume limit, and we proceed to work in the
limit $h=1$.''
\end{srcfact}

\emph{(vii$'$) Printed use of the quantifier by the source (corroboration).}  The following
passages show the source stating the cutoff-uniform quantifier of \eqref{eq:UGJS} and
consuming it for arbitrary cutoff functions of its class, not only in the limit $h\to1$.  The
source's $V(g)$ is the interaction $\mathcal U_g$ of item~(i); its
$\langle F\rangle_h$ is $\int F\,dq_h$.
\begin{srcfactstar}[{\cite[pp.~594--597 and 629]{GJS}}]
\emph{(a) Proof of Theorem 1.1.1, pp.~594--595.}  ``For test functions
$f_i\in C_0^\infty(\mathcal O)$ and for cutoff functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, we assert that
\[
 \Bigl|\int\prod_i\Phi(f_i)\,dq_{h_1}-\int\prod_i\Phi(f_i)\,dq_{h_2}\Bigr|
 \le 0(1)e^{-m_1d/2}
 \tag{1.1.11}
\]
[sic: p.~594 prints the prefactor of (1.1.11) with an upright digit zero, ``0(1)'', where
the $O(1)$ of (1.1.10) on the same page is meant; transcribed as printed since 7 November
2026] where $d=\operatorname{dist}(\mathcal O,\operatorname{suppt}\,h_1-h_2)$, and then
Theorem 1.1.1 follows.  To prove (1.1.11) let $g=h_2-h_1$, and define
$g_i=g\chi_{\Delta_i}$, where $\chi_{\Delta_i}$ is the characteristic function of
$\Delta_i$.  Also we use the notation $\langle F\rangle_h=\int F\,dq_h$, and set
$Q=\prod_i\Phi(f_i)$.  Then
\begin{align*}
 \langle Q\rangle_{h_2}-\langle Q\rangle_{h_1}
 &=\int_0^1d\alpha\,\frac{d}{d\alpha}\langle Q\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}\\
 &=-\int_0^1d\alpha\bigl[\langle QV(g)\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}
   -\langle Q\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}\langle V(g)\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}\bigr]
 \tag{1.1.12}\\
 &=-\int_0^1d\alpha\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^2}\bigl[\langle QV(g_i)\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}
   -\langle Q\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}\langle V(g_i)\rangle_{h_1+\alpha g}\bigr] .
\end{align*}
We apply Theorem 1.1.7 to each term in the sum to obtain
\[
 |\langle Q\rangle_{h_2}-\langle Q\rangle_{h_1}|
 \le\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^2\cap\operatorname{supp}g}
 O(1)e^{-m_1\operatorname{dist}(\mathcal O,\Delta_i)}
 \le O(1)e^{-m_1d/2} .
\]
As a special case, the cutoff Schwinger functions $S_h$ converge as $h\to1$.''

\emph{(b) Proof of Theorem 1.1.7, pp.~596--597.}  ``Proof of Theorem 1.1.7, assuming
Theorems 1.1.8 and 1.1.11.  Take $n=0$ in Theorem 1.1.11 Then $Q$ is a polynomial of
degree zero, i.\ e., a constant.  From the choice $B=I$, it follows that
\[
 Q=\int A\,dq_h+O(1)\|A\|e^{-m_0(1-\varepsilon)T} .
\]
After rotating and translating the strip separating $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ in Theorem 1.1.7,
and after choosing $A=Q_1$, $B_T=Q_2$ in Theorem 1.1.11, the proof follows from Theorem
1.1.8, (1.1.16) and the above determination of $Q$.''  The estimate (1.1.16), p.~596,
reads ``$|\int(A-Q)B_T\,dq_h|\le O(1)\|A\|\,\|B\|e^{-\gamma T}$, uniformly in $h$.''

\emph{(c) p.~629.}  ``Theorem 1.1.11 follows from this inequality, while Theorem 1.1.8
is the special case $B=I$, $n=0$.''  The uniformity sentence of the same page is Source
Fact~\ref{sf:printed}.
\end{srcfactstar}

\emph{(viii) Scaling.} The unitary space-time dilation of \cite[p.~590]{GJS} sends
$(m_0,\lambda)$ to $(s^{-1}m_0,s^{-2}\lambda)$; the exact reduction of the dimensionless
smallness hypothesis to the printed one is Proposition~\ref{prop:scaling}.

\emph{Scope.} Every item of this assumption is a printed statement of \cite{GJS}, used at
the scope at which it is printed; this is the standard under which
Assumptions~\ref{A:cutoff}--\ref{A:covar} are imported, and no stricter one is available
to this manuscript, since the printed proof of Theorem 1.1.7 itself obtains its
$h$-independent constant from Theorem 1.1.8 at the same $h$ (p.~597) while Theorem
1.1.8 is printed only ``uniformly as $h\to1$'' (p.~595).  Four points of scope are
recorded.
\emph{(a) Item (vi), retired.}  From 16 August to 30 October 2026 the slab-uniform estimate
\eqref{eq:UGJS} was carried as a named hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:MAIN}, documented
on 5 September 2026 as the quantifier the source states on p.~629 and consumes on
pp.~594--597 (items (vii), (vii$'$)) but ``assembled from four pages of the source rather
than read off one theorem''.  The source fact of item (vi) shows that it is read off one printed theorem,
Theorem 1.1.11, whose estimate (1.1.16) is printed ``uniformly in $h$'', in the
specialization the source itself prints as its proof of Theorem 1.1.8; the reading of
5 September 2026 used the same pages as evidence for Theorem 1.1.8 and is the same
mathematics with different bookkeeping.  Accordingly, from 31 October 2026, item (vi) was
imported as printed and Theorem~\ref{thm:MAIN} no longer carried it as a separate
hypothesis; that was a re-sourcing, not a proof.  Since 7 November 2026 item (vi) is no
longer used: Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} derives the moment bounds of
\S\S\ref{sec:M2} and~\ref{sec:G} from item (iv) with Lemma~\ref{lem:Z},
Lemma~\ref{lem:uv} and Theorem~\ref{thm:stability}, so that Theorem 1.1.7 is the one
theorem of the source imported.  The manuscript still does not re-derive the cluster
expansion; Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} audits the source mechanism and proves the analytic
prerequisites that Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} consumes.  Items (v)--(vii$'$) are kept
as provenance.
\emph{(b) Item (iv).}  GJS Theorem 1.1.7 is printed for localized monomials separated by a
strip of any orientation (p.~594).  Its printed proof rotates the strip into the time
direction (p.~597) and so reaches sharp-time monomials only across strips parallel to the
time-zero line.  Lemma~\ref{lem:ce2strip} uses only that case; Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}
also uses the transverse case, listed separately as A8(iv)-T.  The price of retiring
item (vi) is therefore that the printed statement of Theorem 1.1.7 is used in that case
(Theorem~\ref{thm:D4}, hence Theorem~\ref{thm:M2} and all that consumes $M$); the uniform gap
of Theorem~\ref{thm:G} rests on the parallel case alone (Lemma~\ref{lem:ce2strip},
Theorem~\ref{thm:D3}).
\emph{(c)} The source's own proof of Theorem 1.1.7 obtains its constant from Theorem 1.1.8
at the same $h$ (p.~597); this manuscript does not re-verify that proof, exactly as it
re-verifies no proof behind Assumptions~\ref{A:cutoff}--\ref{A:covar}.
\emph{(d) Readings made explicit.}  Theorem 1.1.7's ``independent of $h$'' is read over
the class of p.~589 (compact support, $0\le h\le1$), the only class of space-time cutoffs
$h$ of the measures $dq_h$ that the source defines; the quantifier ``uniformly in $h$'' of
(1.1.16), in the retired item (vi), was read the same way, and p.~629 states the
uniformity of Theorems 1.1.8 and 1.1.11 ``in the space cutoff $h$''
(Source Fact~\ref{sf:printed}).  The constants $O(1)$ of (1.1.10) and (1.1.16) are read as
depending on the standing thresholds (and, for (1.1.16), on $n$ and $\varepsilon$) only,
not on $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $A$, $B$, $T$ or $h$, as the source's $O(1)$ is read throughout this
manuscript (Source Facts~\ref{sf:CE2}--\ref{sf:CE1}); \S\ref{sec:G} needs this for
observables of unbounded total degree.  The stability input (2.4.34) of the source's proof
(Appendix~\ref{app:huniform}, M6) enters Theorem 1.1.7; under the import standard it
belongs to the proof this manuscript does not re-verify.  The monomials (1.1.5)--(1.1.6),
which GJS print as formal integrals with ``${:}\ {:}$'' denoting ``Wick order with respect
to the measure $d\Phi$'' (p.~589), are read as the objects constructed in
Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} (Definition~\ref{aux:d1-obs}), and the source's $V(h)$ of
(1.8), p.~589, as the $\mathcal U_h$ of Assumption~\ref{A:stability}
(Remark~\ref{aux:notation-gjslattice}(iv)); items 1 and 10 of \texttt{part\_i/C5\_reading\_record.md}
ask a human reader to confirm the printed text these readings rest on (the definition (1.8) on
p.~589; the forms (1.1.5)--(1.1.6) on pp.~593 and 595).  The formerly
illegible norm prefactor was settled by page-image inspection: $K_1$ enters to the first
power and the local weight is $K_2^{2N(\Delta)}$ (gate R2, \texttt{m4/r2-check.tex}).  All
constants in this manuscript use the exact reading \eqref{eq:printednorm}.

\emph{Used in.} \S\ref{sec:reduction} (scaling), \S\ref{sec:slab}, \S\ref{sec:M2}
(items (ii)--(iii): Steps~1--4), \S\ref{sec:norms} (norms), \S\ref{sec:G} (CE2, parallel case), Appendix~\ref{app:huniform},
Appendix~\ref{app:comparison} (CE2 in both orientations; items (i)--(iii)); items (v),
(vi), (vii) and (vii$'$) are used in no proof.

\texttt{gjs-theorems-10/11/12}, \texttt{gjs-core-11/12}, \texttt{gjs-uniform-46},
\texttt{gjs-uniformity-46}, \texttt{gjs-proof-14} (E20--E26, E54);
\texttt{gjs-thm1111-13} (p.~596), \texttt{gjs-proof118-17} (p.~600), \texttt{gjs-thm41-45}
(p.~628), added 31 October 2026.\par}

results.label: prop:scaling
results.title: dimensionless weak-coupling reduction
results.statement:
The standing inequality $0\le\lambda/m_0^2<\varepsilon_{\mathscr P}$ implies the source
smallness hypothesis of Assumption~\ref{A:gjs}. More precisely, the GJS unitary dilation
with $s=m_0/M_*$ sends
\[
  (m_0,\lambda)\longmapsto
  (s^{-1}m_0,s^{-2}\lambda)
  =\left(M_*,\frac{M_*^2}{m_0^2}\lambda\right),
\]
and the transformed coupling is strictly smaller than $\lambda_*$.

results.label: rem:wlog
results.title: coordinate convention and transport of the conclusions
results.statement:
The dilation behind Proposition~\ref{prop:scaling} identifies the model at
$(m_0,\lambda)$ with the model at $(M_*,\lambda')$, $\lambda'=(M_*/m_0)^2\lambda
<\lambda_*$, as follows. Let $s=m_0/M_*$, $y=sx$, and let $\sigma_s$ be the scaling
automorphism of the Weyl algebra, $\sigma_s(W(f,h))=W(s^{-1}f(\cdot/s),h(\cdot/s))$
(a symplectic map). The sharp-time covariance is scale-covariant between the two masses,
$C_{M_*}(s\,z)=C_{m_0}(z)$ (the one-dimensional analogue of the substitution in the
proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:scaling}), so $\sigma_s$ carries the mass-$m_0$ Fock
state onto the mass-$M_*$ Fock state and is unitarily implemented by some $U_s$ with
$U_s\Om_0^{(m_0)}=\Om_0^{(M_*)}$; moreover $\sigma_s(\A(O))=\A(sO)$. On the
generators, $\mu_{M_*}(k/s)=s^{-1}\mu_{m_0}(k)$ (since $sM_*=m_0$) gives
$U_sH_0^{(m_0)}U_s^*=s\,H_0^{(M_*)}$, and the Euclidean Wick identification of
Proposition~\ref{prop:scaling}, restricted to sharp time (Remark~\ref{rem:conv}), gives
$U_sV_{m_0,\lambda}(g)U_s^*=s\,V_{M_*,\lambda'}(g(\cdot/s))$; hence
\[
 U_s\,K_{m_0,\lambda}(g)\,U_s^*=s\,K_{M_*,\lambda'}(g(\cdot/s)),
 \qquad g\in\CH .
\]
Consequently $g\mapsto g(\cdot/s)$ is an order isomorphism of $\G$ onto $\G$ (and a
bijection of $\CH$), cutoff ground states correspond under $U_s$, and the two cutoff
nets of states are carried onto each other. Every conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:MAIN}, proved in the working (scaled) coordinates, therefore holds for
the original model with the dictionary: localization $O\leftrightarrow sO$; plateau
distance $d\leftrightarrow s\,d$, so the rate becomes $\Psi_{m_{1,*}}(s\,d)$, again
decaying faster than every inverse power of $d$; dynamics
$\alpha_t\leftrightarrow\alpha_{st}$, the light cone being form-invariant; gap
$m_1:=s\,m_{1,*}$; and the local-moment clause of item (5) transports to supports of
length $2/s$ --- equivalently, it holds for supports of length $2$ after splitting $h$
by a partition of unity into at most $\lceil s\rceil+1$ pieces of support length
$\le2/s$ (finite additivity of $V$), with constant $(\lceil s\rceil+1)$ times the
transported one. All displayed constants of \S\S\ref{sec:slab}--\ref{sec:lppl} and of
Appendices~\ref{app:constants}, \ref{app:huniform} and~\ref{app:comparison} are the constants
of the working coordinates, in which the unit-lattice geometry of Assumption~\ref{A:gjs} is literal.

has $L>0$, since $f\ne0$). Then
\[
 \E_{\mu_g}\bigl[X_f^{2n}\bigr]\le A_f\,K_f^{2n}\,(2n)! \qquad(n\ge1),
\]

\[

 \le2\max\{1,A_f\}\sum_{n=0}^\infty(sK_f)^{2n}<\infty
 \qquad(0\le s<1/K_f) .
\]
$A_f$ and $K_f$ do not depend on $n$; $A_f$ depends on $g$ (through $N_g$, $N_B$) and on
$I$, $K_f$ on $f$, on $I$ (through $N_I$), on $K_2$ and on $m_0$, and not on $g$.

section.title: Ground state, invariances, and the Main Theorem
section.label: sec:ground

results.statement:
Let $0\le\lambda/m_0^2<\varepsilon_{\mathscr P}$. Then there is a state $\omega_\infty$ on
$\A$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)] \emph{(full-net convergence with rate)} for every bounded open interval $O$,
      $\lim_{g\in\G}\|(\omega_g-\omega_\infty)|_{\A(O)}\|=0$, and
      $\|(\omega_g-\omega_\infty)|_{\A(O)}\|\le\Psi_{m_1}(d)$ whenever $g\equiv1$ on $O_d$,
      with $\Psi_{m_1}$ decaying faster than every inverse power;
\item[\rm(2)] \emph{(local normality)} $\omega_\infty|_{\A(O)}$ is normal for every $O$;
\item[\rm(3)] \emph{(ground state)} $\omega_\infty$ is a ground state of $(\A,\alpha)$ in the
      spectral sense;
\item[\rm(4)] \emph{(invariances)} $\omega_\infty\circ\tau_a=\omega_\infty$ for all $a\in\R$;
      and for even $\mathscr P$, $\omega_\infty\circ\theta=\omega_\infty$;
\item[\rm(5)] \emph{(spectra and local moment)}
      \[
       \spec H(g)\subseteq\{0\}\cup[m_1,\infty)\quad(g\in\CH),
       \qquad \dim\ker H(g)=1,
      \]
      and $\sup_{g\in\CH}\|V(h)\Om_g\|\le M$ for real $h$ with $\|h\|_\infty\le1$ supported
      in an interval of length $2$.
\end{enumerate}
The weak-coupling estimate imported is one printed theorem of \cite{GJS}: Theorem 1.1.7
(Source Fact~\ref{sf:CE2}), used at its printed scope, including the transverse case
A8(iv)-T of Assumption~\ref{A:gjs} for the sharp-time observable of Theorem~\ref{thm:M2},
a case the printed statement covers and the printed proof does not reach.  The uniform
local moment and the moment bounds behind the uniform gap are theorems of this manuscript
(Theorems~\ref{thm:D3} and~\ref{thm:D4}, Appendix~\ref{app:comparison}), proved from
Theorem 1.1.7, the normalization Lemma~\ref{lem:Z}, the ultraviolet Lemma~\ref{lem:uv} and
the stability Theorem~\ref{thm:stability} of Appendix~\ref{app:huniform}, and the
constructions of the Wick powers recorded in Assumptions~\ref{A:cutoff}
and~\ref{A:stability}; the former moment input, Theorem 1.1.11 (Assumption~\ref{A:gjs}(vi)),
is retired.  Appendix~\ref{app:huniform} does not re-derive the cluster expansion.  In
addition, the proof uses the separately identified standard cutoff-construction inputs of
Assumptions~\ref{A:cutoff}--\ref{A:covar}.  Proposition~\ref{prop:scaling} verifies that the
dimensionless weak-coupling hypothesis implies the source smallness condition. The theorem
is an implication from exactly this list of printed statements; no other external input is
used.  The constant $M$ of item (5), and through it the rate $\Psi_{m_1}$ of item (1),
contain the finite, unevaluated constant $S_2(B_{3\times5})$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:stability}.

results.statement:
The GJS phase-transition and mean-field papers \cite{GJS75,GJS76} prove the existence of
phase transitions and of two pure phases in specified strong-coupling regimes. As cited
here, they are context: they do not, by themselves, supply the full Hamiltonian
phase-space classification (B1)--(B4) --- in particular not the midpoint identification
(B4) --- for the state space of $(\A,\alpha)$. This manuscript therefore makes no
unconditional assertion that its state space carries the structure of
Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:broken}; Theorem~\ref{thm:dichotomy} says only that, at weak coupling,
that structure cannot coexist with the cutoff-uniform gap. The two rigorous options
recorded by the audit --- state (B1)--(B4) explicitly, or delete the corollary --- are
resolved here by the first.

results.label: lem:wick
results.title: Wick lower bound; the $h\ge0$ entry
results.statement:
With
\begin{gather*}
 C(\mathscr P):=\sum_{n=0}^{2p'}|a_n|\max_{0\le j\le n/2}\frac{n!}{j!\,(n-2j)!\,2^j},\\
 C_{p'}:=\max\Bigl\{1,\ \max_{1\le m<2p'}\frac{2p'-m}{2p'}\,(2m)^{m/(2p'-m)}\Bigr\},
\end{gather*}
\[
 b(\mathscr P):=C_{p'}\sum_{m=0}^{2p'-1}C(\mathscr P)^{2p'/(2p'-m)}\,a_{2p'}^{-m/(2p'-m)} ,
\]
one has ${:}\mathscr P{:}_c(x)\ge-b(\mathscr P)\,(1+c)^{p'}$ for all $c\ge0$ and $x\in\R$.
Consequently, for every $h\in\CE$ with $\supp h\subseteq\Lambda$ and every $\kappa\ge2$,
\[
  \mathcal U_{h,\kappa}\ \ge\
  -\lambda\,b(\mathscr P)\,|\Lambda|\,\bigl(1+C_*+\tfrac1{2\pi}\log\kappa\bigr)^{p'}
  \ \ge\ -c_1\,(\log\kappa)^{p'},
\]
\[
  c_1:=\max\Bigl\{1,\ \lambda\,b(\mathscr P)\,|\Lambda|\Bigl(\frac{1+C_*}{\log2}+\frac1{2\pi}
  \Bigr)^{p'}\Bigr\}>0 ,
\]
with $C_*$ of \eqref{eq:ckappa}; $c_1$ depends on $\lambda$, $\mathscr P$, $|\Lambda|$, $m_0$
and $\|\delta\|_\infty$ (the last two through $C_*$), and the maximum with $1$ makes
$c_1\ge1$, which the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:stability} uses (for its threshold $b_1$).

results.label: lem:uv
results.title: ultraviolet difference; the $h\le1$ entry
results.statement:
For $n\ge1$ and $R\ge0$ put
\begin{gather*}
 A_n:=16\pi\Bigl[(4\pi)^{-n}2^{n-1}\bigl((b_0+2)^n+2^{n+1}n!\bigr)+3\bigl(\|\delta\|_\infty
 (b_0+2)\bigr)^n\Bigr],\\
 L_m(R):=\int_0^R\bigl(b_0+2+2|\log r|\bigr)^m\,dr\ \ (m\ge0),\qquad
 B_n(R):=12\,n\,(4\pi)^{-(n-1)}L_{n-1}(R),\\
 c_2:=\lambda^2|\Lambda|\sum_{n=1}^{2p'}a_n^2\,n!\Bigl[\frac{A_n}2\Bigl(1+\frac1{\log2}\Bigr)^n
 (\log2)^{n-2p'}+B_n(R)\,(\log2)^{-2p'}\Bigr] .
\end{gather*}
Then for all $h\in\CE$ with $\supp h\subseteq\Lambda$, $R=\operatorname{diam}\Lambda$, and all
$\kappa\ge2$,
\[
  \bigl\|\mathcal U_h-\mathcal U_{h,\kappa}\bigr\|_{L^2(d\mu_0)}^2
  \ \le\ c_2\,\kappa^{-1}(\log\kappa)^{2p'} .
\]
The constant $c_2$ depends on $\lambda$, $\mathscr P$, $|\Lambda|$, $\operatorname{diam}
\Lambda$, $m_0$ (through $b_0$) and $\|\delta\|_\infty$, and on nothing else; every
$L_m(R)$ is finite, the logarithmic singularity being integrable.

results.label: thm:stability
results.title: $h$-uniform stability
results.statement:
For every $p<\infty$ and compact $\Lambda$,
\[
  \sup\bigl\{\|e^{-\mathcal U_h}\|_{L^p(d\mu_0)}\ :\ h\in\CE,\
  \supp h\subseteq\Lambda\bigr\}\ \le\ \bigl(1+e^{pb_*}\bigr)^{1/p}<\infty ,
\]
where $b_*=b_*(p,p',c_1,c_2)$ is the threshold defined in the proof, with $c_1$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:wick} and $c_2$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:uv}.  The bound depends on $\Lambda$ only
through $|\Lambda|$ and $\operatorname{diam}\Lambda$ (monotonically), and otherwise on
$p$, $\lambda$, $\mathscr P$, $m_0$ and $\|\delta\|_\infty$; in particular it is the same
for all translates of $\Lambda$.

results.label: rem:whyclass
results.title: why the class is what it is
results.statement:
The two halves of the constraint $0\le h\le1$ are used in complementary places:
positivity in the pointwise lower bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:wick} would fail for $h$ of
variable sign --- the interaction density is unbounded above \emph{and} below), and
boundedness in the $L^2$ kernel estimate (Lemma~\ref{lem:uv}) and in M3; the upper bound
also enters, through $\int h\le|\Lambda|$, in Lemmas~\ref{lem:Z} and~\ref{lem:wick}.
Nothing else about
$h$ --- smoothness, shape, time extent, monotonicity along a sequence --- is touched in
Lemmas~\ref{lem:wick}--\ref{lem:uv} or in M3; the stability input of the source's own proof
(M6) is a separate matter. This is the structural content of Source Fact~\ref{sf:printed}.

results.statement:
Assume the standing assumption of \S\ref{sub:d2-conv}.  Let $F=\sum_{a\in\mathfrak A}F_a$ be a
finite sum of localized monomials $F_a$ of type (1.1.5) or (1.1.6) \cite[p.~593]{GJS}, with
kernels in $L^2$ and every individual degree $n_i<\bar n$, and put
$\GJS{F}:=\sum_{a\in\mathfrak A}\GJS{F_a}$, the norm (1.1.9) of this decomposition.  Let $R$
be a non-empty finite set of squares containing every localization square of every $F_a$, let
$B\supseteq R$ be a box, let $h\in\CE$, and let $\mathcal D:=\mathcal D(h,B)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(a)] Suppose that to every $\Delta\in\mathcal D$ a strip $S_\Delta$ of positive width
$w_\Delta$ separating $\Delta$ from $\bigcup R$ is assigned.  Then
\[
 \bigl|\ev{F}{h}-\ev{F}{h^B}\bigr|\le C_7\,c_U\,\GJS{F}\sum_{\Delta\in\mathcal D}e^{-m_1w_\Delta} .
\]
Every estimate behind this bound is Source Fact~\ref{sf:CE2} (GJS (1.1.10)) for a pair
$(F_a,U_{\Delta,n})$, across the strip $S_\Delta$, at a cutoff $h_\alpha\in\CE$; the
orientation of $S_\Delta$ is the orientation of that application.  If $S_\Delta$ is transverse
to the time-zero line and $F_a$ is of type (1.1.5), that application is the transverse case of
GJS Theorem~1.1.7, used at the printed statement's scope and listed as A8(iv)-T
(Assumption~\ref{A:gjs}, item (iv-T)).
\item[\rm(b)] (A form of the statement of \texttt{ugjs/PLAN.md}, Part~1, with positive widths;
the plan's form does not require positive width.)  If every square $\Delta\not\subseteq B$
meeting $\supp h$ is separated from $\bigcup R$ by a strip of positive width, then
\[
 \bigl|\ev{F}{h}-\ev{F}{h^B}\bigr|\le C_7\,c_U\,\GJS{F}
 \sum_{\Delta\not\subseteq B,\ \Delta\cap\supp h\ne\varnothing}e^{-m_1d(\Delta,R)} .
\]
The widest strips used here are not controlled in orientation
(Remark~\ref{aux:d2-uses}(2)); where one is transverse to the time-zero line and some $F_a$
is of type (1.1.5), form (b) uses the transverse case of GJS Theorem~1.1.7 at the printed
statement's scope (A8(iv)-T, Assumption~\ref{A:gjs}, item (iv-T)).
\end{enumerate}
The constants $C_7$ and $m_1$ are those of Theorem~1.1.7 in working coordinates (Remark~\ref{rem:wlog}), and $c_U$ is that of Lemma~\ref{aux:notation-cU}; none depends on $h$, $B$, $R$ or
$F$.

Assume the standing assumption of \S\ref{sub:d2-conv}.  Let $g\in\CH$, let $I\subset\R$ be a
bounded interval of positive length, let $s\in\R$, and let $l_s$, $N_g$, $N_B$, $B=B_s(g,I)$ be
as in \S\ref{sub:d3-setting}.  Let $F=\sum_\beta c_\beta Q_\beta$ be a finite real linear
combination of cylinder monomials supported in $I$, and $F(s)$ its value at sharp time $s$.
Then for every $T>0$,
\[
 \Bigl|\int F(s)\,dq_{h_{T,g}}\Bigr|\le A\,\|F\|_{L^2(\dphi)}+B'\,\GJS{F(s)} ,
\]
\[
 A:=e^{3\lambda|a_0|N_B}\,S_2(B),\qquad
 B':=2\,C_7\,c_U\,N_g\,\frac{e^{-m_1}}{1-e^{-m_1}} ,
\]
where $S_2(B)$ is the constant of Definition~\ref{aux:notation-S2def}.  The norm $\GJS{F(s)}$
is that of the decomposition in Lemma~\ref{aux:d3-cyl}(v), which bounds it in terms of the
functions $f_{\beta,i}$.  In working coordinates (Remark~\ref{rem:wlog}), the constant $A$
depends only on $(\lambda,\mathscr P,m_0)$ and on $N_B$, through the unevaluated constant $S_2$;
the constant $B'$ depends only on $C_7$, $m_1$, $K_1$, $K_2$, $\lambda$, $\mathscr P$ and $N_g$.
Both are independent of $T$ and $s$, and $B'$ is independent of $I$.
